transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2025-07-08 15:00 EDT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Ava (Redwood AE), Liam (Redwood SE), Maya (Redwood CSM), Nadia (Harborline Head of Risk), Tom (Infra), Priya (Legal Ops), Ethan (Platform)

Summary:
Quick intake to understand Harborline's constraints for deploying LLM inference; primary focus on cross-border data flows, legal hold/long-term retention for financial disputes, and whether Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private fits their compliance posture. Asked for evidence and network diagram; agreed next steps.

Topics:
- Data residency and cross-border routing
- Log retention, legal-hold and e-discovery paths
- Encryption/KMS and key residency expectations
- Network egress and VPC/private control plane options
- Proof points (SOC2/HIPAA) and sample configs for review

Transcript:
00:00 Ava: hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you taking the time, um we're here to try and map where Redwood could fit into Harborline's stack and specifically the residency/legal hold constraints.
00:23 Nadia: yeah thanks Ava, quick context — we have a couple regulatory cases where we need to retain transcripts and some inference outputs for up to seven years, and sometimes we have to produce them cross border for litigation, so that is the big sticky bit.
00:45 Liam: got it, and when you say retain, is that raw request/response logs, or redacted artifacts? just so we're aligned.
01:02 Nadia: so it's a mix — for some disputes legal wants full fidelity, for others redacted. we also have tiered retention, 90 days hot, then long term cold, but legal can flag a case and we have to hold earlier deletions.
01:22 Priya: right and our question is, do you provide a legal-hold mechanism that prevents deletion from the storage layer, and can that be scoped to an account or tenant?
01:35 Ava: yes — we have patterns for that, I mean the basic options are Hosted API, Dedicated reserved pools, or Private (VPC/on‑prem). each has tradeoffs for control over retention and audit evidence.
01:52 Ethan: quick Q — Hosted's easiest, but is the control plane in the US only? because we handle EU customers and we can't have egress out of eu for eu-subject data.
02:07 Liam: currently Redwood's hosted is region aware; we can pin inference to an EU region and we also offer Dedicated instances in region. full private deployment gives you control of the control plane too, for strict residency.
02:24 Tom: when you say Dedicated, is that single-tenant hw or just reserved capacity? what logs are we able to see?
02:38 Ava: Dedicated is a reserved capacity pool for your account — it's isolated from multi-tenant noise but it's still operated by Redwood. we stream audit logs and per-request metadata to your logging endpoints, and you can opt to have no request bodies forwarded to our control plane.
02:57 Nadia: there's often confusion with the words, sorry, when you say 'audit logs' does that include input prompts?
03:07 Liam: we can export structured telemetry (latency, tokens, model id) and full request/response separately. for customers with retention concerns we support redaction at ingestion and also can route raw artifacts to customer-owned storage in Private.
03:25 Priya: and encryption for those artifacts — do keys stay in our KMS?
03:34 Ava: with Private deployments we support customer-managed keys — K M S slash H S M integration — and for Dedicated we support bring-your-own-keys in certain configurations, though the control plane still has minimal metadata.
03:51 Tom: if we went Hosted pinned in eu-west-1, what's your evidence package for SOC2 or HIPAA? we need chain of custody statements.
04:05 Maya: we'll send the SOC2 plus a HIPAA summary, and an evidence map that ties regions to storage buckets and retention policies — that's part of the post-call package.
04:18 Nadia: perfect. also, legal hold — we need a way to elevate a case and stop scheduled deletions across whatever tiering you have. is that an API or a manual process?
04:32 Liam: we expose a legal-hold API in Private and Dedicated roadmaps; for Hosted there's a support process today but customers can integrate with our retention flags via API for automated holds. some customers run a small job to flip hold flags in the control plane.
04:50 Priya: just flagging regulators will want to see who accessed keys and who requested the hold. can you produce those access logs?
04:59 Ava: yes — access logs are included in audit trails; we'll export admin actions and key usage events to your SIEM. sometimes the naming is off in transcription, we call the admin audit stream 'ctrl-plane-admin-events' in our docs.
05:18 Ethan: about data in flight — egress to third-party tokenizers or embeddings? do you call out to external APIs?
05:30 Liam: by default no; we run inference locally on the model runtime. for some features like external retrieval or third-party plugins, those calls are explicit and you can disable them.
05:44 Tom: network level: do you publish static outbound IPs for Dedicated so our firewall teams can whitelabel?
05:54 Ava: yes, we provide egress IP ranges for Dedicated and for Private it's inside your VPC so it's your IPs. Hosted has regional egress ranges and we'll provide a list — we'll include that in the config template.
06:12 Nadia: retention lengths — the compliance team wants to avoid long tail token storage, can we configure token-level retention separate from message metadata?
06:25 Liam: we have multiple layers: per-request bodies, KV cache, telemetry. token-level data in KV caches is ephemeral by design but you can prevent caching. request bodies are configurable to be stored or not.
06:39 Priya: litigation hold could be indefinite, how do you manage storage costs for that?
06:47 Maya: typically customers export held artifacts to their cold storage (e.g., S3 with legal hold tag) and Redwood can stop deletion triggers; we don't bill for their reproduction in your archived buckets beyond egress and storage.
07:03 Ethan: about indexing for e-discovery — if legal needs to search across transcripts, do you provide a search index or do we maintain that?
07:15 Liam: we have optional indexing as a paid addon that creates a search-friendly index and can be stored in your account; otherwise customers export raw files and index in their own tools.
07:29 Tom: ok, slightly different question — when you say 'Private' do you mean a private control plane or fully air-gapped on‑prem?
07:40 Ava: both options exist. Private can be VPC-hosted control plane with customer-managed networking, or a fully on‑prem bundle for air-gapped setups. the latter requires additional professional services.
07:55 Nadia: we have subsidiaries in singapore and germany — regulatory wants to know cross-border operator access. can you restrict Redwood staff from seeing customer data?
08:07 Liam: yes, in Dedicated and Private we can switch off service-level access; for Hosted we have strict role based access control and can provide audit evidence of any access. Private on-prem gives you complete operator isolation.
08:24 Priya: what about data residency metadata — if a request originates in UK but model is served in eu-west, does metadata show both?
08:36 Ava: metadata includes request origin, model region, and processing region. we also support geofence routing policies so requests from UK can be forced to UK-region models.
08:50 Ethan: latency targets — if we pin to eu-west, what SLOs do you offer?
08:58 Liam: Dedicated gives SLOs for p95 latency; hosted has best-effort regional latency numbers in our catalog. we'll attach a performance spreadsheet in the follow-up.
09:15 Priya: a legal nuance — record-keeping rules require us to show chain of custody for key rotations; do you support exportable key rotation logs?
09:26 Ava: yes, key rotation events can be exported; K M S events from your KMS + our control plane admin events will show the timeline.
09:36 Tom: are there any known blockers for us to do a private deployment in eu-germany region? we're on Azure EMEA, and need physical residency in an azure germany region.
09:49 Liam: we have worked with Azure and can deploy into customer VPCs in that region; there are lead times for on‑prem racks though. we'll need to scope network peering and OLA.
10:03 Nadia: thank you. switching to legal: Priya has a couple questions on retention policy language we use in contracts — do you have DSA templates that call out legal hold and log retention?
10:16 Maya: yes we have DSA/DSC templates and we can provide redlines for Harborline. we'll attach a sample that shows retention clauses and data export commitments.
10:30 Priya: perfect, we'll need that to take to procurement. also — any third party subprocessors? where are your subprocessors located?
10:42 Ava: we'll list subprocessors by region in the packet; main ones are cloud provider infra in selected regions and a small set of observability providers. we'll include a map.
10:55 Ethan: quick operational: do you provide a replay tool for reproducing requests for debugging, and can that be disabled?
11:05 Liam: yes, we have a replay/debug capture that can be turned off; customers can opt to never persist request bodies in the control plane.
11:16 Tom: outstanding question from infra — how do you handle PII redaction automatically?
11:24 Liam: we offer optional PII redaction at ingestion using deterministic scrubbers, plus customers can supply their own redaction rules before forwarding. accuracy varies so legal often wants both automated and manual review.
11:38 Nadia: in the event of a data subject request under GDPR, do you provide tooling to locate and delete all records for a subject across archives and indices?
11:50 Ava: we provide a data subject access request (DSAR) playbook and tooling to query tenant-scoped data; for cold archives you may need to coordinate with your archive indexing, we can help produce an export for deletion.
12:07 Priya: ok thank you, this is helpful. can we go through an example flow — say there's a fraud case flagged, legal wants to preserve everything for user X, what's the steps end-to-end?
12:19 Tom: (laughs) role play time.
12:22 Liam: step 1: legal creates a hold via API or support ticket; step 2: control plane marks all related artifacts as non-deletable and triggers export to cold storage; step 3: admin events and key usage are captured and exported; step 4: we provide manifest and hash list for chain of custody.
12:49 Priya: do you hash full request bodies? that's often asked.
12:55 Ava: yes we can provide content hashes and manifests for forensic integrity. sometimes transcription hits the product name weirdly, but it's standard.
13:08 Ethan: great. one more thing — regulator wants to know if any operators outside eu could access data during maintenance windows.
13:18 Liam: for Private on-prem, no. for Dedicated we can sign operational playbooks that prohibit operator access outside europe and we can provide egress-limited ops windows. for Hosted, we maintain role restrictions and can provide evidence.
13:33 Nadia: timeline question — if we ran a pilot, what's the fastest path?
13:40 Ava: pilot path: 1) Hosted pinned region with redaction flags for 2–4 weeks, or 2) Dedicated reserved pool trial (4–8 weeks) if you need more control. Private on‑prem is usually 8–12+ weeks.
13:58 Tom: what's the expected cost delta between Hosted vs Dedicated roughly?
14:05 Maya: depends on throughput; ballpark Dedicated is higher fixed cost but lower per-request cost at scale. we'll include a basic calc sheet.
14:18 Priya: can you give an example clause for legal hold wording we can use?
14:26 Maya: we'll include suggested contract language in the DSA sample.
14:32 Tom: ok if no more high level, maybe we go into specifics — I'll share our network diagram and legal will share retention policy.
14:40 Ava: perfect. quick recap?
14:44 Nadia: send SOC2/HIPAA + evidence map; include subprocessors and egress IP ranges; share DSA sample and retention clause; provide Dedicated latency spreadsheet and demo slot; Tom/Ethan will share network diagram and list of outbound ports.
15:02 Ava: sounds good — action items we'll follow up in email and set the demo. huge thanks everyone.

End of transcript.
